goal: A round never acts on a plan that `main` has replaced, and a workarea that cannot take `main` is reported as a project waiting on hands rather than as a plan that is stopped.

Today a conflict anywhere in the merge makes the round read the plan out of the branch instead of out of `main`, and then report whatever that older plan says. Measured 2026-09-05: `docx-editor` reported *"step 17 is blocked on decision docx-ime-input-source"* for eight consecutive rounds (runner.log 23348–23566). No such step exists on main — #11383 replaced it the evening before, and the plan on `origin/main` has said `ready` since. The only conflicting file was `docs/technical/docx-editing-surface.md`, which has nothing to do with the plan.
contract: The documented contract is what this restores, not a new rule: *"What a planning session and the runner share is a `PLAN.json` on `main`, and nothing else"* (`docs/project/README.md`, § Who writes what).

`fromHead` keeps the case it was built for. Its reasoning at `src/mc/run.js:336` is sound where it applies — a worktree with a merge in progress may carry conflict markers in the plan itself, and HEAD is then the branch's last good copy. Nothing here removes that; what changes is when it fires.
A conflicted merge is still not resolved by the round and still not the round's to resolve. `syncMain` aborting is correct behaviour and stays.

A step session's own edits to its plan in its worktree are untouched. This is about which copy the *round* reads to decide what to hand out, not about what the session then edits or what its pull request carries.
out_of_scope: Resolving any particular workarea's conflict by hand. `~/mc/docx-editor/memoro` was already brought to `docx-editor-3` from `origin/main` on 2026-09-05, and the estate's other stuck worktrees are a person's, one at a time.
How a repair session resolves a merge, and the one-repair rule. #617 and #618 changed that ground days ago and this project reads it rather than moving it.

The plan-conflict rule itself (`src/mc/plan-merge.js`). `resolvePlanConflict` and `mergePlanText` decide who may write what in a conflicted plan; this project changes only which file the round reads when the rule could not resolve one.

`mc status`'s own choice of which copy to read. `status-project.js` deliberately reads the workarea's tree when there is one and says so when the two differ; that is a different question with a different answer and it is not opened here.

success_criteria.criterion: A round whose merge conflicted in a file that is not the plan hands out the step `origin/main` says, not the step the branch says.
success_criteria.check: A test drives a round with a conflict in one non-plan path and a plan that differs between HEAD and `origin/main`, and asserts the step chosen is main's. Failing today with the branch's step.

success_criteria.criterion: A workarea that could not be brought to base is reported as such, by name, and not as whatever its stale plan said.
success_criteria.check: Read `runner.log` after a round over a genuinely conflicted workarea: the project-level line names the workarea and the files, and no line reports a blocker read out of the stale plan.

success_criteria.criterion: The case `fromHead` exists for still works.
success_criteria.check: A test with the conflict in the `PLAN.json` itself asserts the plan is read from HEAD and the step session is handed the merge, exactly as today.

success_criteria.criterion: A workarea stuck this way is visible without reading `runner.log`.
success_criteria.check: With one workarea deliberately unable to take main, it is named in the brief or in `mc status` with the files it conflicts on. Run the surface and read it.

documents.label: Where the plan is read and the round decides
Who shares what with the runner
The sibling reading of what the runner can act on

steps.title: Put the choice to Martin, with the narrow fix measured
steps.done_when: The PR names the three options, says which the code supports and at what cost, and carries one recommendation; Martin's answer is written into `docs/project/mc/rulings.md` when he gives it.
instruction: This step writes no fix. It exists because the thing to change is a **deliberate, documented choice**, and a session that quietly reverses one is how a reason gets lost. `run.js:336` argues for reading HEAD in its own words: *"HEAD is the branch's last good copy, and it is the right one: the step being handed out is the step this branch is on. Main's own edits to the plan are what the session is merging in."* Read that comment in full before writing anything.

Then read the condition it is attached to. At `run.js:1265` the call is `planOf(worktree, name, { fromHead: conflicts.length > 0 })`, and `conflicts` is `syncMain`'s *remaining* unresolved list (`run.js:431`) — every file git could not merge and the plan's own rule did not resolve. It fires on **any** conflicting file. The docstring's justification covers exactly one of them: a conflicted `PLAN.json`. That mismatch is the whole defect, and it is worth stating in one sentence in the PR, because it makes the narrow fix obvious: `fromHead` should fire when the plan itself is among the conflicts, not when anything is. `isPlanPath` (`src/mc/plan-merge.js:159`) is the predicate and it is already imported into `run.js`.

Both cases are live and both are in `runner.log`, so name them as the two ends of the range. `docx-editor`, eight rounds from 04:51 to 06:25 on 2026-09-05: the only conflict was `docs/technical/docx-editing-surface.md`, the plan was not conflicted at all, and the round reported a blocker from a step main had already replaced. `sdk-artifact-storage`, 08:03:56 the same day: *"PLAN.json is not resolvable by the plan's rule — steps[1]: changed on this branch and on main both"*, then the conflict, then `step 2 is blocked on decision sdk-storage-deploy-verified`. In the second the plan **is** the conflicted file and `fromHead` is doing what it was built to do.

Put the three options with the cost of each. **1 — read the plan from `origin/main`, never from the worktree**: honours the documented contract, `git show origin/main:<path>` is the same call the `step-parallelism` blocked audit already made (read it at `git show 914ce4b^:docs/project/mc/step-parallelism/blocked-audit.md`; it was archived in #573 and opens by naming this exact hazard), and it removes the class — but it also removes `fromHead`'s legitimate case, so say what a step session is then handed when its plan is genuinely mid-merge. **2 — refuse the step when the worktree could not be brought to base**: cheaper, keeps the current read, turns a silent wrong answer into a loud one, and does not fix the answer. **3 — the narrow scoping above plus 2 as its guard**: `fromHead` fires only on a conflicted plan, everything else reads main, and a workarea that cannot take main says so as a project-level stop.

Recommend one. The proposal recommended 1 with 2 as a guard; the scoping finding above was not available to it, and 3 may now be the smaller and more honest change. Decide from the code, not from the proposal, and say which you chose and why.

Carry the answer into `docs/project/mc/rulings.md` in the shape that file already uses — the question, the options, Martin's answer quoted verbatim, and the step that builds it. mc keeps no record of a decision anywhere else, so the ruling and this plan are the only two places it survives.

steps.title: The round reads the plan the contract says it shares
steps.done_when: The round hands out the step `origin/main` names, except in whatever case step 1's ruling preserved, and a test covers both sides of that line.
instruction: Build what step 1 settled and nothing else. If the ruling was option 3, the change at `run.js:1265` is one predicate — `conflicts.some(isPlanPath)` in place of `conflicts.length > 0` — plus whatever step 1 decided about reading `origin/main` rather than the worktree file in the clean case. If it was option 1, `planOf` grows a read through `git show origin/main:<path>` and `fromHead` goes; say in the PR what a mid-merge step session is handed instead.

`planOf` (`run.js:347`) already builds the repository-relative path as `['docs', 'project', programme, name, 'PLAN.json'].join('/')` for its `git show HEAD:` call, so the same string serves `git show origin/main:`. The programme is discovered by walking `docs/project` in the worktree — that walk stays, because it is how the project's directory is found at all.

A read from `origin/main` can fail in ways a file read cannot: the ref may be behind if the fetch failed, and the path may not exist on main at all for a project whose plan has not landed yet. `syncMain` already returns `{ ok: false, conflicts: [] }` for a failed fetch and the round skips on it (`run.js:1260`), so the ref is fresh whenever this is reached — say so in a comment rather than adding a second fetch. A plan that is not on main is a case `repoOf` and `assembleQueue` already exclude; assert that rather than handling it twice.

Update the docstring at `run.js:336` to say what is now true. It is a good comment that has become a wrong one, and the next reader will trust it — that is how this defect survived. Whichever case survives, name it and name what it is not.

Two tests, both driving the round rather than `planOf` alone: a conflict in a non-plan path with HEAD and main disagreeing about the plan, asserting main's step is handed out; and a conflict in the `PLAN.json` itself, asserting the behaviour step 1's ruling preserved. `tests/mc/run.test.js` already fixtures the round with injected `deps` and has conflict cases at `:928` — extend that shape.
`npm test`.

steps.title: A workarea that cannot take main says so, once, where somebody looks
steps.done_when: A workarea whose merge of `origin/main` aborted is reported as a project waiting on hands, with the conflicting files, and is visible without reading `runner.log`.
instruction: This is step 1's option 2 — the guard — and it is worth having whichever way the ruling went, because a worktree that will not take main is a thing a person has to fix either way and today nothing tells them so.

The round already writes the line. `abandonMerge` at `run.js:1272` says `<name>: <why> — the merge of origin/main is aborted, still conflicting in: <files>`, and it is correct as far as it goes. What it lacks is a reader: it went to `runner.log` eight times for `docx-editor` and nobody saw it. The defect is the audience, not the sentence.

The sibling project `runner-visibility` builds the reading this belongs in — one function beside `kindFor` in `src/mc/status-collect.js` answering "would the runner start this project now, and if not what is in the way", with an aborted merge as one of its reasons, surfaced in `mc status`, on the page and in the brief. **Check whether that has landed before you build anything here.** If it has, this step adds the reason to it and nothing else; if it has not, add the smallest thing that puts a stuck workarea where a person looks, and say in the PR which you did so the two do not end up with two implementations of one reason.

Say it once, not once per round. `runner.log` already carries 9 827 `, skip` lines and a per-round line for a condition that lasts eight rounds is what made this invisible in the first place. A surface that shows current state, with a `since`, is the right shape; a log line per round is not.
Verify against a real one: make a workarea conflict with main by hand, let a round run, read the surface, then clean it up. Put what it printed in the PR.
`npm test`.

steps.title: Close out
steps.done_when: `docs/technical/mc-run.md` says which copy of a plan the round reads and when, and `docs/project/project_log.md` has the row.
instruction: Write down which copy the round reads, in which case, and why — this is the fact that was true, documented, deliberate, and wrong at the same time, and the documentation is where the next person deciding to change it will look.

Say it beside the contract it serves: the planning session and the runner share a `PLAN.json` on `main` and nothing else. `docs/project/README.md` already carries that sentence; the technical doc should say how the runner honours it.
Add the row to `docs/project/project_log.md`.
